key_concepts: Earth's surface is mostly water, with a smaller percentage of land.
The Northern Hemisphere is the land hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere is the water he
Earth's internal layers are inner core, outer core, mantle, and crust.
The crust is Earth's outermost solid rock layer.
The crust is classified into continental crust and oceanic crust.
Continental crust is thicker, less dense, and made mostly of granitic rocks.
Oceanic crust is thinner, denser, and made mostly of basaltic rocks.
Oceanic crust underlies ocean basins and has mid-ocean ridges, deep-sea trenches, and unde
Seafloor spreading and subduction continually create and destroy oceanic crust.
When oceanic and continental crust collide, the denser oceanic crust subducts.
Landforms can be classified according to whether they are on oceanic or continental crust.
Density is the ratio of mass to volume and can be found by water displacement.
